curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8841-1/ (scans; the buggy is pages 3-6, steps 1-15, the tractor after)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column runs down through a universal joint to an 8-tooth pinion on a toothed rack, and the rack pushes both steering arms.
Rolling the buggy works the engine's piston: a pin in the 24-tooth gear on the left rear axle is a crank, and a connecting rod pushes the piston up and down in its block behind the seat.
functions.source: book: steps 3-5 (the inset in step 4 shows the pin in the gear); that rolling drives it is inferred, as the gear only sits on the left rear axle

functions.does: The front wheels turn freely on pins in the steering arms.
The rear wheels are on two separate axles; only the left one turns the engine.
functions.note: inferred: the right rear axle turns on its own and drives nothing

functions.does: The roll cage, the seat and the steering column's mounting stay rigid: the toothed toggle joints hold their angle, and the cage is a closed frame.
functions.source: inferred: steps 10-14 build the cage from toothed toggle joints, which click and hold, and the seat folds round its hinge axle only while it is built
functions.note: KineBrick today lets the front cage strut p35 3706 (or the column holder p32 3705) be dragged, turning the 10-long axle p28 3737 it hangs on; the rest of the cage and the seat don't move
